title: External-duality comparison respects open composition of a support map
statement:
Fix the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Work in the finite-Tor constructible categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ with the canonical ordinary and exceptional adjunctions and composition comparisons of [def-trf-admissibility]. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to Z=X\times_sX$ a correspondence [def-trf-correspondence], $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and $j:W\hookrightarrow C$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $P=K\boxtimes_A^L D_XK$ using [def-trf-external-product, def-trf-dualizing-complex], write $U=Lp_2^*K$ and $V=Rp_1^!K$ on $Z$, and put $H_c=R\mathcal Hom_A(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K)$ and $H_{cj}=R\mathcal Hom_A(L(c_2j)^*K,R(c_1j)^!K)$ [def-trf-trace-class-source]. The pullback and exceptional composition comparisons identify $H_{cj}$ with $R\mathcal Hom_A(Lj^*Lc_2^*K,Rj^!Rc_1^!K)$. Let $\delta:R\mathcal Hom_A(U,V)\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ be the canonical external-duality map of [thm-trf-verdier-duality], and let $\iota_h:H_h\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Lh^*U,Rh^!V)$ be the canonical pullback/compositor identification for $h=c,cj$. Denote the exceptional internal-Hom exchange of [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange] under this identification by $E_j:H_{cj}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!H_c$. The external-duality comparisons are explicitly the canonical composites
$$\xi_h:=Rh^!(\delta)\circ E_h\circ\iota_h:H_h\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh^!P\qquad(h=c,cj),$$
where $E_h$ is the exceptional internal-Hom exchange for $h$. If $\kappa:R(cj)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!Rc^!$ is the specified composition comparison, then
$$\kappa_P\circ\xi_{cj}=Rj^!(\xi_c)\circ E_j.$$
This is equality of the canonical maps, with no additional symmetry permutation or sign.

source.place: §0.3(a)-(b), equations (0.3)-(0.4), and §1.2.2(a), first arrow: compatibility with open composition.

proof.text: Write $Z=X\times_sX$, $U=Lp_2^*K$, and $V=Rp_1^!K$ on $Z$, and let $\delta:R\mathcal Hom_A(U,V)\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ be the canonical external-duality map. For $h=c,cj$, the pullback and exceptional composition comparisons give the canonical identification $\iota_h:H_h\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Lh^*U,Rh^!V)$; for $h=c$ this uses $Lc^*U\simeq Lc_2^*K$ (the pullback compositor $c_{c,p_2}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]) and $Rc^!V\simeq Rc_1^!K$ (the exceptional compositor of [def-trf-admissibility]), and for $h=cj$ the same compositors for $p_2cj$ and $p_1cj$. Thus the displayed formula $\xi_h=Rh^!(\delta)\circ E_h\circ\iota_h$ is the actual canonical map, with $E_h$ the exceptional internal-Hom exchange at $(U,V)$. The admissibility hypotheses and [thm-trf-verdier-duality] put all objects in the required finite-Tor constructible domains. Let $\theta:R\mathcal Hom_A(L(cj)^*U,R(cj)^!V)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Lj^*Lc^*U,Rj^!Rc^!V)$ be the compositor identification for $cj=c\circ j$. The two ways of identifying $H_{cj}$ with $R\mathcal Hom_A(Lj^*Lc^*U,Rj^!Rc^!V)$ agree: (i) $\theta\circ\iota_{cj}$, and (ii) the statement's identification $H_{cj}\simeq R\mathcal Hom_A(Lj^*Lc_2^*K,Rj^!Rc_1^!K)$ followed by $Lj^*$ and $Rj^!$ of the two components of $\iota_c$. In the first variable this is associativity of the pullback compositors for $j,c,p_2$: by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] every compositor is, on a K-flat complex with flat terms (a class preserved by the pullbacks), the class of the termwise canonical isomorphism of module pullbacks, and these termwise isomorphisms are associative because each is the unique comparison of composite inverse images given by their adjunctions. In the second variable it is associativity of the exceptional compositors for $j,c,p_1$: these are the conjugates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of the compact-support compositors, which are associative by the associativity clause of [thm-sf-comp-composition], and conjugation is a bijection compatible with composition. In particular, no independent choice of $\iota_{cj}$ is being made.

Put $Q=R\mathcal Hom_A(U,V)$ and write $E_h^{\rm raw}$ for the exchange of [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange] at the displayed objects. Naturality of the composition comparison $\kappa$ at $\delta:Q\to P$ (it is a natural isomorphism by [def-trf-admissibility], the conjugate of the natural $\alpha$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]) gives
$$\kappa_P\circ R(cj)^!(\delta)=Rj^!Rc^!(\delta)\circ\kappa_Q.$$
The composition-coherence lemma [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-composition], applied to $c,j,M=U,N=V$, gives, with $\theta$ of Step 1,
$$\kappa_Q\circ E_{cj}^{\rm raw}=Rj^!(E_c^{\rm raw})\circ E_j^{\rm raw}\circ\theta,$$
where $E_{cj}^{\rm raw}$ starts from $R\mathcal Hom_A(L(cj)^*U,R(cj)^!V)$, $E_c^{\rm raw}$ from $R\mathcal Hom_A(Lc^*U,Rc^!V)$ and $E_j^{\rm raw}$ is the exchange for $j$ at $(Lc^*U,Rc^!V)$. The exchange $E_j:H_{cj}\to Rj^!H_c$ named in the statement is the exchange for $j$ at $(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K)$, precomposed with the statement's identification of $H_{cj}$. The exchange for $j$ is natural in both variables (contravariantly in the first), so applying it along the two components of $\iota_c$ and using the agreement (i)=(ii) of Step 1 gives
$$Rj^!(\iota_c)\circ E_j=E_j^{\rm raw}\circ\theta\circ\iota_{cj}:H_{cj}\to Rj^!R\mathcal Hom_A(Lc^*U,Rc^!V).$$
Substituting these equalities into the explicit formula for $\xi_{cj}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}\kappa_P\circ\xi_{cj}
&=Rj^!Rc^!(\delta)\circ\kappa_Q\circ E_{cj}^{\rm raw}\circ\iota_{cj}\\
&=Rj^!Rc^!(\delta)\circ Rj^!(E_c^{\rm raw})\circ E_j^{\rm raw}\circ\theta\circ\iota_{cj}\\
&=Rj^!Rc^!(\delta)\circ Rj^!(E_c^{\rm raw})\circ Rj^!(\iota_c)\circ E_j\\
&=Rj^!\bigl(Rc^!(\delta)\circ E_c^{\rm raw}\circ\iota_c\bigr)\circ E_j=Rj^!(\xi_c)\circ E_j.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the equality is an equality of the specified canonical maps; the only compositor coherences used are the associativities of Step 1.

The preceding calculation proves the required identity. Since $\delta$, every $E_h$ and $\iota_h$, and the composition comparisons are canonical isomorphisms, both sides have the displayed source and target and are defined on the stated constructible domains. The order of the external product remains $P=K\boxtimes_A^LD_XK$ throughout, so no symmetry permutation or sign is introduced. For $W=\varnothing$ or $W=C$, for $K=0$, and for identity $c$, the same compositor calculation specializes to the corresponding unit identities.

split_report.summary: Repair of the returned split. I made the external comparison explicit as xi_h = Rh!(delta) composed with the exceptional internal-Hom exchange and the canonical pullback/compositor identification. The proof now establishes the identity directly from naturality of the exceptional composition compositor at delta, the helper composition-coherence equality, naturality of exchange in both variables, and associativity of the compact-support compositors. The previous transpose/open-mate argument was removed; the external-product order and edge cases remain explicit. Maintainer review (2026-10-18): corrected the direction of the transported exchange formula in Step 2 (Rj^!(iota_c) composed with E_j equals E_j^raw after theta and iota_cj), made the compositor identification theta explicit, and cited the pullback-compositor node and the conjugation calculus for the associativity used in Step 1.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the extracted compatibility clause in the proof of lem-trf-local-term-locality: the open restriction comparison in Varshavsky §0.3(a)-(b), equations (0.3)-(0.4), used before the contracting-correspondence argument. The added helper realizes the composition-coherence subargument that the returned proof had left implicit.

tool_uses.why: Its naturality and associativity supply the coherence of the exceptional composition comparisons and of the pullback/compositor identifications used in the direct calculation.

Step 1 needs the pullback compositor L(gf)^*=Lf^*Lg^* and its termwise description to identify L(cj)^*Lp_2^*K with Lj^*Lc_2^*K coherently; no node of sk-i-curve-zero or its cited units states the pro-etale derived pullback composition isomorphism (thm-trf-verdier-duality uses the same node for Lc_2^*K=Lc^*U).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q34-77d59825e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the mathematics in full. The item and the new node lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-composition are both true. The helper is a general coherence lemma for any M, N: it does not mention P, delta or the correspondence. It is not a duplicate of lem-trf-open-hom-mate, sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom/lem-sf-tensor-hom, lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas or lem-sc-left-adjoint-composition-iso-associativity, and it does not restate the item. Source checks: Varshavsky §0.3(a)-(b) (0.1)-(0.3), §0.4 (0.4) and §1.2.2(a). The explicit formula xi_h = Rh^!(delta) o E_h o iota_h agrees with steps 5-7 of thm-trf-verdier-duality (delta = kappa^-1). The coefficient category D^b_ctf(-,A_{E,n}) and the conjugate compositors of def-trf-admissibility are used throughout, with no symmetry sign. The conclusion is exactly the identity (2) used by lem-trf-trace-class-open-restriction. I fixed three faults: (1) C1/E5: Step 1 needs associativity of the pullback compositors and attributed it to thm-sf-comp-composition, which covers only Rf_!. It now cites lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, declared as a tool use (the same node thm-trf-verdier-duality uses), and def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate for the exceptional side. (2) E4/E5: the Step 2 formula E_j = Rj^!(iota_c) o E_j^raw o iota_cj had the wrong type. It is corrected to Rj^!(iota_c) o E_j = E_j^raw o theta o iota_cj, with the compositor theta made explicit, and the computation is rewritten one equality per fact.
